answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because summit only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, cedar is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any karst approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
